newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean shipbuilders go limit up on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean shipbuilders go limit up on strong yen.

text.p: Share prices of South Korea's top three shipbuilders, including Daewoo Heavy Industries Co, went limit-up in Monday's morning trading on the yen's strength against the dollar, analysts said.
Daewoo gained 400 won to 5,400, while Hanjin Heavy Industries rose 640 to 8,690 and Samsung Heavy Industries rose 670 to 9,120.
"Right now market sentiment in Korea is that the strengthening yen is good for Korean shipbuilders," said Vince Kim, shipbuilding analyst for Jardine Fleming Securities.
The yen leapt as high as 117.60 yen to the dollar in early Monday trading in Tokyo, compared with 123.11/21 yen at late afternoon on Friday. At mid-morning, the yen stood at 118.45/50.
A stronger yen helps South Korea's exports because Korean goods compete mainly with Japanese goods in world markets.
The competition is especially strong in shipbuilding where Japan and South Korea, ranked first and second respectively, account for about 70 percent of the world market.
Shipbuilding shares also benefitted from Korea's current competitiveness against Japan on delivery, Kim said.
Japan's order book is filled for two years, while Korean shipbuilders still have some availability, he said.
"The impatience on the part of ship owners to take delivery of their ships earlier should help Korea," Kim said.

However, he said the market's positive response to shipbuilders was an overreaction. Prices should move in response to earnings and only Hanjin was likely to see improved earnings this year, Kim said.
